newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan urges envoys to check Kuwait abuse reports.
newsitem.headline: Jordan urges envoys to check Kuwait abuse reports.

text.p: King Hussein of Jordan on Thursday asked Western envoys to investigate reports of beatings of Jordanian prisoners by security men in a Kuwaiti jail.
The state news agency Petra said the king made the request in a meeting with the U.S. and British ambassadors in Amman.

The king conveyed to the ambassadors his "interest in the situation, circumstances and the conditions of arrest of these prisoners as well as the true picture of the conditions of these Jordanian citizens," Petra said.

"His Majesty emphasised the need (by Kuwait) to abide by all international conventions and norms and to adhere to laws that regulate the detention of individuals," Petra quoted the king as saying in his first public comment on a human right report.

The Arab Organisation for Human Rights in Jordan said on Thursday it had received a report that 400 Kuwaiti security men carrying clubs and sticks beat inmates for three hours in a wing of Salbiya prison in Kuwait housing more than 100 prisoners.
It said they were then left outside in the cold for three hours. Their money, belongings and books were taken, it said.
It did not say whether it had been able to verify the report.
A Jordanian official said the government, which has had no embassy in Kuwait since the two countries fell out during the 1990-91 Gulf War, was trying to check the report through third parties.
Kuwait dismissed reports of the beatings as "lies" and said they were aimed at "defaming the state of Kuwait".

"Kuwait is extremely keen on safeguarding human rights guaranteed by our Islamic religion," a Kuwaiti official said, noting that officials from the International Committee of the Red Cross have unconditional access to Kuwaiti prisons.
